President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s administration is still not done with its flurry of subpoenas stemming from the Sept. 21 protest—this time invoking sedition, a silencing tactic harking back to Spanish colonial rule. 

Jacob Baluyot, associate editor of Polytechnic University of the Philippines’ The Catalyst and national chairperson of PUP’s publication alliance, and Bagong Alyansang Makabayan President Renato Reyes Jr. received summons from the state over charges of sedition, inciting to sedition, and violations of the cybercrime law.

The summons followed a barrage of subpoenas around late October against youth activists present during the Baha sa Luneta rally. Less than a month into 2026, police have now issued seven subpoenas in total—marking the first known instance in this issue of the police serving two separate summons on a single individual.
